reviewCriteria: Do not assume every customer wants a brighter room
Separate lightness, contrast, visual weight and privacy requirements

transcript.customer: Our sitting room is small and quite dark. Must I have white curtains?

advice.text:
No, white curtains aren’t a must. In a small, dark sitting room, curtains close to the wall colour can soften contrast and make the room feel less divided. A warm oatmeal or muted colour may feel gentler than bright white, depending on your furnishings.

Alternatively, deeper curtains can create a cosy, enveloping feel, though with a stronger presence around the window. Keeping them clear of the glass when open helps preserve the daylight you have.

alternatives: Curtains close to the wall colour for softer contrast.
Deeper curtains for a cosier atmosphere and stronger window presence.

transcript.customer: I actually enjoy a cosy, enveloping room and dislike stark white.

advice.text:
Then there’s no need to aim for a bright, airy look. A deeper, muted curtain colour could support the cosy atmosphere you enjoy, especially if it sits close to the wall colour rather than creating a sharp contrast.

A softly textured plain would bring warmth without much visual activity. Alternatively, a restrained pattern could add character, though it would make the curtains more noticeable in a small room.

transcript.customer: Could we keep that mood but avoid everything feeling heavy?

advice.text:
Yes. Cosiness can come from soft colour and texture rather than very dark, dense fabric. I’d lean towards a muted mid-tone with a matte, softly woven finish, keeping the contrast with your walls gentle. That can feel enveloping without making the window too dominant.

A restrained, open pattern is another option if a plain feels flat, though it adds more visual activity. Allowing the curtains to sit clear of the glass when open will also help preserve daylight.
advice.patternDirection: Plain, or a restrained pattern with plenty of open space for a little more character.
advice.textureDirection: Softly woven, matte texture rather than a dense or strongly lustrous finish.
alternatives: A restrained, open pattern adds character but creates more visual activity than a textured plain.
